review_notes: I read the whole file. I looked for repeated reasoning across hom_ext_of_single, shiftAut_pow_single, modelN_injective and modelHom_injective. The only real duplication is the decomposition of v as a product of single-coordinate elements, which is proved twice. The other similar-looking patterns (by_cases on coordinates, the omega case splits on a.val and m) are short or differ in substance. I did not compile anything. Moving eq_prod_single above hom_ext_of_single is safe because it depends only on the Multiplicative toAdd API and Finset.univ_sum_single, and it needs no later declarations.

findings.excerpt: have hv : v = ∏ i, Multiplicative.ofAdd (Pi.single i (v.toAdd i)) := by
findings.problem: The decomposition of an element of Multiplicative (Fin n → ZMod 3) as the product of its single-coordinate components is proved inline inside hom_ext_of_single. The same argument is proved again, with the same steps, in the later lemma eq_prod_single. Both use Multiplicative.toAdd.injective, rw [toAdd_prod], simp only [toAdd_ofAdd] and exact (Finset.univ_sum_single _).symm. The two proofs can drift apart, and the earlier one never uses the named lemma.
findings.proposed_change: Move eq_prod_single above hom_ext_of_single, keeping its statement and proof unchanged. In hom_ext_of_single, replace the inline hv block with `rw [eq_prod_single v]`, or with `have hv := eq_prod_single v`. The rest of the proof stays as it is: `exact Subgroup.prod_mem _ fun i _ => Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨(i, _), rfl⟩`. The `classical` call that eq_prod_single already carries can stay there. modelN_injective already uses eq_prod_single, so after the change the decomposition is proved once and used in both places.
findings.benefit: The product decomposition has one proof and one name. hom_ext_of_single becomes shorter, and a reader sees that the same fact drives both the hom-extensionality argument and the injectivity argument.

evidence.excerpt:
theorem eq_prod_single (v : Multiplicative (Fin n → ZMod 3)) :
    v = ∏ j, Multiplicative.ofAdd (Pi.single j (v.toAdd j))
